name: Triggers Workflow
description: The completion of one workflow fires another (`on: workflow_run: workflows: [<name>]`). Points from the workflow that completes to the workflow that runs as a result, even though the declaration lives on the target: the source's run is what initiates the target's. This is the two-stage shape GitHub's own docs recommend for untrusted input — an unprivileged `pull_request` stage whose completion fires a privileged base-repository stage — and therefore the edge along which a fork's data reaches a workflow that holds secrets.

trigger_event.description: The event class. An enum of one today so a later cross-workflow trigger (`repository_dispatch`, a `workflow_dispatch` fired by another workflow's job) can join without renaming the edge.

declared_name.description: The upstream workflow's display name exactly as the target's file wrote it. Kept so a rename of the upstream shows as drift here rather than as a silently dead trigger.

types.description: `types:` as written (`completed`, `requested`, `in_progress`). Absent when the file omits it — GitHub then defaults to requested and completed, and that default is NOT written here because the file did not declare it.

branches.description: `branches:` filter as written on the upstream run's head branch; absent when omitted.
